title: THz-Driven Quantum Ionic Magnetism in a Quantum Paraelectric SrTiO3
authors: In Hyeok Choi, Sergei Urazhdin, Man Tou Wong, Zi-Jie Liu, Keith A. Nelson
abstract: Magnetic moments carried by rotating ionic motion in crystals are becoming recognized as an important contribution to magnetism, angular momentum transport, and optical activity. However, efficient approaches to their dynamical control are lacking. Here, we report THz-driven generation and optical detection of quantum ionic magnetism in quantum paraelectric SrTiO3. We observe an oscillatory ionic magnetization without a corresponding oscillatory polarization, contradicting from the classical relation M~PXdP/dt while its suppression above the quantum paraelectric regime points to a quantum ionic origin. Analysis shows that this effect results from the beating between quantum ionic eigenstates whose degeneracy is lifted due to the directional symmetry breaking by the THz pulse. The presented approach provides a pathway for the ultrafast control of ionic magnetization in quantum materials for spintronic and thermotronic applications.
summary: This paper reports the detection and characterization of quantum ionic magnetism in SrTiO3 using THz-pumped nonlinear optical techniques. By observing oscillatory magnetization that defies classical predictions, the authors confirm that the effect originates from quantum beating between ionic eigenstates. This work establishes a method for ultrafast control of ionic magnetism crucial for advanced spintronic and thermotronic applications.
main_problem: The study investigates the generation and ultrafast control of quantum ionic magnetism in the quantum paraelectric material SrTiO3.
main_result: The research observes oscillatory ionic magnetization that persists beyond the relaxation time of polarization oscillations, confirming a quantum mechanical origin distinct from classical electro-optic effects.
method: The authors combine THz-pump-induced Second Harmonic Generation Circular Dichroism (SHG-CD) measurements with theoretical modeling using density matrix formalism.
model_or_system: The system is quantum paraelectric SrTiO3, whose dynamics are modeled using the density matrix formalism, considering ionic displacements in a double-well or four-well potential. The THz pulse drives the system, probing coherence between ionic eigenstates.
key_observables: THz-helicity-dependent $\Delta	ext{ICD}$ and $\Delta	ext{ISHG}$ signals, fast ($\sim 1 	ext{ THz}$) and slow ($\sim 0.2 	ext{ THz}$) oscillatory components, and the time-domain decay of ionic magnetization.
important_parameters: Low temperatures (10 K), the quantum paraelectric regime, and the temperature dependence of the slow oscillation frequency ($\sim (1-T/T^*)^{0.5}$ with $T^* \approx 60 	ext{ K}$).
main_assumptions: The fast oscillations are attributed to the quantum ionic effect rather than purely non-magnetic contributions, and the slow oscillation's temperature dependence is linked to polar nanodomain evolution.
figures_summary: Figures show time-domain THz-helicity-dependent $\Delta	ext{ICD}$ signals, frequency analysis (FFT) confirming fast and slow oscillations, and temperature dependence plots illustrating the decay of these oscillations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical problem, presents THz-CD measurements showing helicity-dependent oscillations, develops a quantum model using the density matrix, and finally compares simulation results (showing slow oscillations persisting after polarization decay) with the experimental observations.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct experimental pathway to observe and control quantum mechanical magnetic moments arising from lattice vibrations (ionic motion) using ultrafast THz pulses, which is highly relevant to understanding emergent magnetism in quantum materials.
